newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump on profit-taking, rates plunge.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump on profit-taking, rates plunge.

text.p: Mexican stocks continued their earlier slump to end off on Wednesday as dealers continued to take profits after what they saw as excessive falls in primary rates, and foreign investors preferred a stronger Dow Jones, traders said.
"We're still adjusting after the huge New Year rally, with sales increasing towards the close, but with volume low as foreigners stayed away today. They preferred Wall Street," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended down 45.14 points, or 1.23 percent, at 3,631.62.
Volume was light at 69.3 million shares traded.
The Dow Jones meanwhile closed up 1.27 percent at 6,740.74 points.
Traders said many dealers feared that primary rates could see a sharp rise up after plunging on Tuesday night to their lowest levels since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis.
Bellwether 28-day Cetes rates fell 102 basis points to 21.91 percent at Tuesday's primary auction.
"The bourse has been weakened since yesterday by a strong Dow Jones, and was further demoralized by the severe drop in primary rates. That's dangerous," a technical analyst said.
"Dealers could think rates have bottomed out and are heading for sharp rises, not slight ones," he added.
Traders and analyst agreed the IPC was heading for support at 3,600 points.

Dealers noted that ADRs listed by market heavyweights Telmex and Televisa bucked the upward trend in the Dow Jones industrial average to close off 1/8 and 1/4, respectively, to 37 and 26. Their L and CPO shares meanwhile fell six centavos and 3.30 pesos, respectively, to 14.52 and 101.70 pesos.
On the broad market, 101 stocks chnaged hands, of which 66 declined while 20 advanced.

Dealers said most leading percentage gainers were second- and third-tier stocks that had moved at small trades, apart from airline holding company Cintra, which gained 10 centavos to 5.50 pesos after brisk trade.

The decliners' list was headed by the Serfin financial group, off 22 centavos at 2.90 pesos. Traders said investor confidence in financial stocks had ebbed since Banacci posted disappointing 1996 earnings results last week.
"Banacci set the pace, and now dealers are dumping financial stocks," a trader said.
